newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends off highs as NY inspires buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends off highs as NY inspires buying.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures closed mostly firmer and in mid-range at the end of the week as a speculator-inspired arabicas rally passed some of its bullish sentiment onto the London market, traders said on Friday. The benchmark March contract closed $11 firmer on the day at $1,245 after touching a high of $1,256, with other forwards also closing above the lows. Volume reached 5,210 lots.

Earlier in the session, trade selling and long liquidation pressured values lower but good buying in New York -- possibly on talk that the USDA had lowered its forecast for Brazil's 1996/997 crop -- spurred sentiment on the robustas, they said.
But then the arabicas market eased when the U.S. authority repeated its forecast for output at 27 million 60-kg bags.
Elsewhere, London traders said fears over a frost in Mexico's coffee areas appeared to have abated, adding that the main risk period had now passed.

"The weather in Mexico is getting better -- the frost was supposed to be last night. If anything, the weather is going to improve," said one. According to Smith Barney, coffee trees in Mexico were spared frost-related damage early on Friday as temperatures held above freezing in key regions.
